label: rem:core-levi-interpretation
title: The millennium problem as contact non-degeneracy at vortex collision
html:
The core-Levi equivalence translates the Navier--Stokes millennium problem strictly into the contact geometry of the underlying brane:

  \text{NS blows up}
  \Longleftrightarrow
  \text{Levi form non-degenerate at collision}
  \Longleftrightarrow
  \kappa(t) = O(1).

Interpretation of each outcome.

If the Levi form remains non-degenerate (\kappa = O(1)): Vorticity mechanically concentrates into tight tubular cores. The absolute lower bound \|\omega\|_\infty \geq c/(T^*-t) holds, triggering BKM divergence and breaking NS regularity. The counter-example successfully executes. The contact structure rigorously defies integrability; the vortex holds as a valid topological defect, producing an unavoidable physical singularity.

If the Levi form degenerates (driving \kappa \to 0 or \infty): Vorticity dissipates into a thin sheet. The structural lower bound fails, leaving NS potentially regular. The contact structure has partially succumbed to integrability exactly at the collision locus, successfully forming a 2-dimensional integral submanifold. Local observability collapses, and the vortex structure devolves into a diffuse smear smoothly absorbed by classical viscosity.

The root-of-unity constraint. Evaluating at q = e^{i\pi/\kappa}, the explicit truncation back to (\kappa-1)/2 modes restricts the core aspect ratio beneath 1 + C(\kappa-1). Sending \kappa \to \infty (q \to 1) diverges this bound, but restricts the divergence exclusively to a linear rate. Biot--Savart stretching propels collision dynamics at \sim 1/(T^*-t). The terminal outcome depends entirely on whether the representation-theoretic bound O(\kappa) outpaces the dynamical rate O(1/(T^*-t)).

The contact-geometric test: does a finite-dimensional approximation over \mathrm{SU}_q(2) preserve Levi form non-degeneracy in the infinite-dimensional limit?
